Careers at Milestone · Oakdale, Minnesota

Join a supportive group practice dedicated to meaningful mental health care for children, adolescents, adults, and families.

Why Milestone

A supportive place to build your practice.

Milestone Mental Health is a group private practice providing specialized mental health care for children, adolescents, adults, and families. As our community's need for care grows, we are seeking providers who want to make a meaningful difference.

Our clinic includes four fully equipped play therapy offices, an observation and coaching therapy room with a one-way window and listening equipment, and individual offices.

Room to grow, with the space and support to focus on meaningful care.

Employment opportunities

Find your place at Milestone.

Explore the position details below. Please contact the clinic to confirm current openings and availability.

Outpatient therapy · Independent contractor

Mental Health Professional or Practitioner

We are seeking mental health professionals or pre-licensed mental health practitioners to provide outpatient services in Oakdale, Minnesota. LPCC, LMFT, LICSW, LADC, or LP credentials are preferred; providers working toward licensure are also encouraged to inquire.

01 / Responsibilities

What you'll do

  • Provide outpatient individual and family therapy.
  • Conduct diagnostic intake assessments.
  • Develop comprehensive treatment plans.
  • Coordinate client care with other providers.
  • Maintain client documentation and treatment notes.

02 / Experience

Preferred experience & interests

  • Experience providing outpatient services; at least one year licensed is preferred, but pre-licensed applicants are welcome.
  • EMDR training or certification, Brainspotting, or Somatic Experiencing.
  • Registered Play Therapist (RPT), or supervision by an RPT-S.
  • Working with children and families, or early childhood (DC 0–5).
  • An interest in developing one of these specializations; professional development support may be available.

Scheduling arrangements

Ways to join the team.

01 / Full-time

Full-time opportunity

One provider comfortable working with adolescents and adults. Up to four days per week, with a caseload of approximately 20–24 clients weekly.

02 / Part-time

Part-time opportunities

Two providers comfortable working with children and adolescents. Up to two or three days per week, with a caseload of approximately 12–18 clients weekly per provider.

Practice support

More support for the work that matters.

Milestone describes the following resources and benefits for its independent contractors, helping providers focus on client care and the growth of their practices.

01 / Compensation

Competitive fee split

A fee split based on monthly revenue, described as up to 70/30.

02 / Operations

Operational support

Referral sources, EHR, insurance credentialing and contracting, billing, balance collection, and MN Care Tax.

03 / Flexibility

Flexible, furnished spaces

Set your own schedule and work from a furnished office or play therapy room.

04 / Resources

Marketing & communications

Advertising and marketing support, plus HIPAA-compliant phone and email systems.

05 / Community

Professional community

Peer consultation, professional collaboration, and possible supervision options for pre-licensed providers.

06 / Development

Continued growth

A sign-on bonus and a stipend for continuing professional development are described among the opportunities.

An opportunity to connect

Purposeful work, with room to grow.

Flexible scheduling, furnished therapy spaces, collaboration with fellow providers, and opportunities for continued professional development.

Interested in joining Milestone? Contact the office to ask about current opportunities.

Specialized support · Children & families

Caregiver Coaching & Consultation.

Understanding a child's emotional or behavioral needs can be challenging. Reflective consultation and in-the-moment coaching can help caregivers find new ways to understand and respond.

Explore Our Approach → Contact Our Office
  1. Home
  2. Specializations
  3. Caregiver Coaching & Consultation

Understanding through reflection

New understanding can shape new responses.

We offer reflective mental health consultation to parents, foster parents, respite providers, childcare providers, and teachers caring for a child with emotional or behavioral challenges.

This consultation supports caregivers in understanding and responding to a child's mental health needs. Reflecting on the child's needs and the relationships involved can help bring new ways of responding to difficult emotions or behaviors into focus.

Space to reflect on what's happening, understand the relationship, and discover new ways forward.

Our approach

Reflective consultation and practical coaching.

Our therapists offer two complementary approaches to supporting caregivers as they navigate challenging emotions, behaviors, and interactions with children.

01 / Consultation

Reflective mental health consultation

Consultation helps caregivers develop a clearer understanding of a child's emotional and behavioral needs, including the relational dynamics that may be influencing an interaction. Through reflection, new ways of responding may become more apparent.

02 / Coaching

In-the-moment caregiver coaching

Our therapists also coach caregivers during caregiver-child interactions. This helps caregivers put new insights about a child's behavior and relationships into practice while developing parenting skills addressed in therapy or consultation.

Who we support

Care for the caregivers, too.

Supporting a child also means supporting the people involved in their everyday care. Caregiver Coaching & Consultation offers room to reflect, build understanding, and practice new responses.

Caregiver support includes

  • Parents
  • Foster parents
  • Respite providers
  • Childcare providers
  • Teachers

Circle of Security Parenting

Understanding COS-P

Building security through connection.

Circle of Security Parenting (COS-P) is an evidence-based intervention for caregivers of children ages 0–12, grounded in decades of research about supporting secure caregiver–child relationships.

Milestone’s therapists use this approach to help parents and caregivers better recognize their children’s emotional needs, respond thoughtfully, and strengthen their relationships.

Understand your child’s emotional world. Support the relationship that helps them grow.

How we support caregivers

What can caregivers explore through COS-P?

The program focuses on helping caregivers reflect on their children’s needs and respond in ways that support emotional security.

01 / Understanding

Recognize emotional needs

Learn to better read a child’s emotional cues and understand what they may be communicating.

02 / Regulation

Support emotional development

Help children manage their emotions and turn to caregivers for support when they need it.

03 / Confidence

Strengthen self-esteem

Encourage a child’s developing sense of self through secure, supportive relationships.

04 / Connection

Trust your caregiving instincts

Honor the wisdom and desire caregivers already bring to helping their children feel secure.

Program options

Support that meets families where they are.

COS-P can be offered within individual or family psychotherapy. Milestone has also periodically offered caregiver groups.

Milestone’s therapists are described as certified COS-P facilitators. Contact the practice to learn about current providers, program formats, and availability.

Our philosophy

Supervision is more than a requirement.

At Milestone, supervision is an opportunity to develop as a therapist in an environment that is validating, supportive, and responsive to your individual needs and stage of professional development.

The approach prioritizes relational safety and meaningful reflection, creating room to bring your genuine self, experiences, and questions into the supervision process.

I believe supervision is a unique and valuable part of the journey of becoming a therapist.

Rachel Milan, MA, LMFT, PMH-C, IMH-E®

Meet your supervisor

Rachel Milan

MA, LMFT, PMH-C, IMH-E®

I am a board-approved supervisor in Minnesota for individuals on the LMFT and LPC/LPCC track.

I believe supervision is a unique and valuable part of the journey of becoming a therapist. I seek to provide a supervision experience that is both validating and supportive, adaptable to your individual needs and stage of development as a therapist. My style of supervision is relational; prioritizing the development and maintenance of safety in the supervision relationship and group that I lead so that you can feel comfortable bringing your genuine self and experiences to the room. I believe group supervision can be a dynamic and powerful experience creating the opportunity to learn not just from me, but from others in a similar stage of professional development.

I have experience working in community-based mental health and private practice settings. My specialties include trauma (trained in TF-CBT, EMDR, Child-Parent Psychotherapy), working with parents, utilizing play in therapy with children of all ages (on track to obtaining RPT), dyadic and relational parent-child work in therapy (trained in Theraplay, PCIT, and CPP), and utilizing knowledge of attachment and development in therapy with individuals of all ages.

Areas of experience and training

  • Trauma & TF-CBT
  • EMDR
  • Child-Parent Psychotherapy
  • Play in therapy
  • Theraplay
  • PCIT
  • Attachment & development
  • Parent-child relationships

Professional development

A supportive space to grow.

Supervision at Milestone is designed to meet developing therapists where they are, with space for reflection, guidance, and learning alongside others.

Experiential Play Therapy

Play is a natural language for children. It gives them opportunities to explore feelings, experiences, and relationships in ways words may not always express.

Explore This Service → Contact Our Office
  1. Home
  2. Child & Adolescents Mental Health
  3. Experiential Play Therapy

Understanding play therapy

The work and language of childhood.

Play is the work and the language of the child. It is a natural part of a child’s daily development to engage in play. Pretend play allows children to explore different identities, feelings, and experiences.

In play, children can have a brave space to lean into feelings and experiences that may be too difficult to address or explore directly.

Through play, children can feel seen, safe, and understood.

What play can make possible

Different ways to explore and express.

Imaginative play can help children explore experiences that may be difficult to describe directly.

01 / Feelings

Explore emotions

Pretend play can offer children a way to explore feelings and experiences.

02 / Experiences

Create meaningful scenarios

Through play, children may create scenarios that reflect real-life situations and themes.

03 / Connection

Invite a therapist into play

A child may invite a therapist to join these scenarios and explore what feels hard to put into words.

What sessions can look like

Making room for the child's experiences.

In experiential play therapy, children create scenarios through play and may invite a therapist into those scenarios to work through real-life situations and themes they cannot easily put into words.

Safety, acceptance, and understanding

Feeling accepted, understood, and safe during play can help children work through experiences connected to challenging emotions or behaviors.

Understanding EMDR

What is EMDR therapy?

Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) is an evidence-based therapeutic approach for individuals of all ages who have experienced trauma or other distressing life experiences.

EMDR is designed to help people process distressing memories. Unlike approaches that rely primarily on talking through an experience in detail, EMDR incorporates bilateral stimulation as part of a structured therapeutic process.

EMDR does not necessarily require recounting every detail of a distressing experience or completing homework between sessions.

When people seek support

When might EMDR be considered?

People may explore EMDR when distressing experiences are connected to emotional, behavioral, or physical challenges. Topics people may discuss with a provider include:

01 / Trauma

Traumatic experiences

Post-traumatic stress, sexual abuse or assault, violence, abuse, and other trauma- or stress-related concerns.

02 / Anxiety

Fear and anxiety

Anxiety, panic attacks, phobias, and performance anxiety.

03 / Mood

Emotional challenges

Depression, bipolar disorders, grief, loss, and distressing emotions.

04 / Daily well-being

Health and sleep concerns

Chronic illness, medical issues, pain, and sleep disturbances.

05 / Complex challenges

Other mental health concerns

Dissociative disorders, eating disorders, and personality disorders.

06 / Recovery

Substance use and addiction

Distressing experiences that may be part of substance-use and addiction-related concerns.

These examples do not mean EMDR is appropriate for every condition or person. Whether this approach fits your needs is something to discuss with a qualified provider.

What treatment involves

How does EMDR work?

EMDR incorporates bilateral stimulation into a therapeutic process that supports the processing of distressing experiences. This may involve several forms of bilateral stimulation:

01 / Visual

Guided eye movements

The therapist may use guided side-to-side eye movements during parts of treatment.

02 / Auditory

Bilateral sounds

Bilateral sounds may be incorporated as part of the therapy process.

03 / Tactile

Alternating tapping

Alternating taps or other tactile cues can be used instead of eye movements.

04 / Individualized

Care tailored to you

A typical EMDR session lasts 60–90 minutes; the approach and course of care depend on individual needs.

How EMDR fits into care

A flexible approach to treatment.

EMDR may be incorporated into ongoing talk therapy, offered as an additional treatment alongside work with another therapist, or used as a stand-alone therapy.

Learn more from the EMDR International Association (opens in a new tab).

Your experience matters.

There is no single timeline that fits everyone. Talk with your provider about what treatment may look like for you.

Our Philosophy

Care begins with connection.

We believe that meaningful growth happens in relationships where people feel safe, supported, and understood.

Whatever challenges bring you here, our team takes time to understand your experiences, honor your strengths, and meet you with compassion. Together, we can strengthen connections, build helpful resources, and navigate life's milestones—one step at a time.

How we can help

Our Services

  • Anxiety

Explore Our Services

Our clinicians can help determine which type of care may be appropriate for you or your family.

Mental Health Diagnostic Assessments

We offer mental health diagnostic assessments to individuals of all ages to determine a diagnosis and provide recommendations for mental health care.

When working with young children (ages 0–5), our therapists have specialized training and experience in the assessment and diagnosis of mental health concerns that may occur during early childhood. To appropriately assess young children, our providers utilize a separate diagnostic manual created for this population. The diagnostic assessment process for children in this stage of development includes a caregiver-only clinical interview, observation of caregiver-child interactions and, whenever possible, an observation of the child in another context such as a childcare or preschool setting.

Neuropsychological Evaluations for Children & Adolescents

We provide neuropsychological evaluations for children and teens when more information is required to understand cognitive, social, emotional, and relational functioning, incorporating knowledge about the childhood and adolescent stage of development.

These evaluations are often sought when there is a desire for diagnostic clarity for mental health concerns or to determine the existence of neurocognitive concerns such as ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder, or Learning Disorders.

Consultation & Coordination of Care

We support coordinated mental health care for clients of all ages. With your permission, we collaborate with other providers involved in your care, including medical providers, medication prescribers, occupational and speech therapists, other mental health professionals, case managers, and skills workers. This collaboration helps align treatment goals, share relevant information, and support continuity of care.

When helpful and desired, we also consult with family members, caregivers, teachers, childcare providers, and other support people. Through consultation, we help those involved in your daily life better understand your mental health needs and develop supportive, consistent ways to respond.

Psychotherapy for Individuals, Couples & Families

We provide psychotherapy for children, adolescents, and adults, as well as couples and families. Our approach is tailored to each client’s needs, stage of life, and goals, with attention to how relationships and life experiences influence emotional well-being.

Our relational services help couples and families strengthen connection, improve communication, navigate conflict and transitions, and address patterns that affect their relationships and mental health.

For young children, therapy includes the direct or close involvement of parents or caregivers. When working with children and adolescents, we partner with caregivers whenever appropriate to support their understanding of their child’s mental health needs and strengthen their ability to respond in helpful, supportive ways.

Virtual Mental Health Care

We offer virtual therapy through a secure, HIPAA-compliant platform, allowing you to attend sessions from a private, comfortable space. Virtual sessions are available for individual, couples, and family therapy when appropriate for your needs. Your clinician can help determine whether virtual care is a good fit. Availability depends on your location at the time of the session and your clinician’s licensing requirements.

Group Therapy

We periodically offer therapeutic and peer support groups that provide opportunities to connect with others, explore shared experiences, and develop skills to support mental health and well-being. Each group is designed for a specific age range, topic, or area of need.

Groups are not currently being offered.

Please check back for future offerings, or contact us to share your interest in a particular type of group. We welcome your ideas and requests!

Focused support

Specializations

Every experience is different. Explore some of the ways our clinicians support children, adults, couples, and families.

Stress, Life Changes & Trauma

Difficult experiences and significant life changes can affect how we feel, relate to others, and navigate daily life. We support children, adolescents, adults, couples, and families experiencing emotional or relational challenges related to stress, loss, change, trauma, or other adverse experiences.

Therapy offers space to make sense of these experiences, build coping skills, strengthen relationships, and work toward greater safety, stability, and well-being. We tailor treatment to each client’s needs, experiences, and goals.

Our therapists are trained in a range of evidence-based approaches to support healing and growth. Depending on your needs and your therapist’s training, treatment may include:

  • Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing (EMDR)
  • Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT)
  • Trauma-Informed Child-Parent Psychotherapy (TI-CPP; CPP)
  • Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT)

Child & Adolescent Mental Health

Children and teens may express emotional distress through changes in their mood, behavior, relationships, or ability to manage everyday demands. We support young people experiencing challenges such as anxiety, difficulty managing emotions, behavioral concerns, school difficulties, reactions to stressors, and conflict with family members or peers.

Our therapists tailor care to each child’s developmental stage, strengths, and needs. Through developmentally appropriate approaches, we help children and teens understand and express their feelings, build coping skills, and strengthen their relationships.

We also partner with parents and caregivers to better understand what may be contributing to these challenges and develop practical ways to respond. Caregiver involvement is tailored to the young person’s age and needs, with attention to supporting trust, growing independence, and connection within the family.

Our therapists draw on a range of therapeutic approaches to support children, teens, and their families. Depending on your family’s needs and your therapist’s training, services may include:

  • Circle of Security Parenting (COS-P)
  • Parent-Child Interaction Therapy
  • Play Therapy
  • Caregiver Coaching & Consultation
  • Social-Emotional Skill Building
  • Sand Tray Therapy
  • Art Therapy
  • Theraplay
  • Trauma-Informed Child-Parent Psychotherapy (TI-CPP)
  • Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT)

Attachment & Relationships

Our relationships shape how we experience connection, trust, and emotional safety throughout life. We support children, adolescents, adults, couples, and families who are navigating relationship challenges, disruptions in close relationships, or patterns that make it difficult to feel understood and connected.

Therapy can help clients explore how past and present relationship experiences influence their emotions, expectations, and interactions with others. Together, we work toward recognizing needs, improving communication, establishing healthy boundaries, navigating conflict, and strengthening connection.

This work may take place in individual, couples, or family therapy. Whether you are exploring your own relationship patterns, strengthening a caregiver-child relationship, or addressing challenges with a partner or family member, we tailor treatment to your needs and goals.

Our therapists are trained in a range of relational approaches. Depending on your needs and your therapist’s training, treatment may include:

  • Theraplay
  • Circle of Security Parenting (COS-P)
  • Couple’s Therapy
  • Family Therapy

Perinatal Mental Health

Did you know, 1 in 7 women and 1 in 10 dads suffer from postpartum depression?

Caring for the mental health of childbearing families during the perinatal period (pregnancy and postpartum) is specialized work that our therapists are passionate about. With a certified perinatal mental health professional on staff, we provide care to families that is knowledgeable and resourceful through this important life milestone.

Scheduling Your First Visit

We're happy to help you schedule an initial appointment or coordinate a 10–15 minute phone consultation with one of our therapists to answer your questions. Call or email us to get started.

Call 651-500-2389 → Email our team →

For privacy, please avoid including sensitive health information in a regular email.

What happens next?

  1. Receive your portal link. Once your intake appointment is scheduled, we'll email you a link to your Secure Client Portal.
  2. Complete your paperwork. You'll complete intake, policy, and financial forms through the portal. Allow approximately 15–20 minutes. Appointment reminders may arrive by email, text, or both.
  3. Prepare for your appointment. Please complete all required forms at least 24 hours before your first visit.

Scheduling & Cancellation Policies

  • If the required intake paperwork is not completed at least 24 hours before your intake appointment, your therapist may cancel and reschedule it until the paperwork is complete.
  • Appointments cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice incur a $75 cancellation fee.
  • If you miss an appointment without notice, the full fee for the scheduled service is required before future appointments can be scheduled. This fee cannot be billed to insurance.
  • All fees and copayments are due at the time of service.

Parent–Child Interaction Therapy.

Parent–Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) helps caregivers learn practical skills while supporting children who experience emotional or behavioral challenges.

Explore PCIT → Contact Our Office
  1. Home
  2. Child & Adolescent Mental Health
  3. Parent–Child Interaction Therapy

Understanding PCIT

Growing connection through guided interactions.

PCIT is an evidence-based therapeutic intervention for young children, typically ages 2–7, who experience emotional and behavioral challenges. Caregivers participate directly in the treatment.

Milestone's therapists are also trained to use developmentally appropriate PCIT adaptations with children ages 8–11.

The work focuses on both the child's needs and the caregiver–child relationship.

When families seek support

Challenges PCIT may help address.

Families may explore PCIT when a child's emotional or behavioral challenges are creating stress at home or in the caregiver–child relationship.

01 / Emotions

Managing strong feelings

Difficulty regulating strong emotions or coping when things do not go as expected.

02 / Guidance

Following directions

Challenges sustaining attention, following directions, or accepting adult guidance.

03 / Anxiety

Responding to worry

Anxious behaviors, including attempts to control surroundings or interactions.

04 / Reactions

Navigating outbursts

Emotional outbursts, aggression, or physical expressions of distress.

05 / Cooperation

Reducing power struggles

Frequent power struggles between a child and caregiver.

06 / Relationships

Supporting family connection

Family relationship distress or a desire for more effective parenting strategies.

What sessions look like

Real-time coaching during play.

During PCIT coaching sessions, you and your child spend time together in a playroom. The therapist observes from a separate room through a one-way window.

Using a small “bug-in-the-ear” device, the therapist offers in-the-moment guidance as you practice skills for understanding and responding to your child's emotions and behavior.

You practice. Your therapist coaches. Together, you build skills during real interactions.

The treatment process

Two phases, with different goals.

PCIT combines relationship-building skills with consistent, supportive ways of responding to challenging behaviors.

01 / Building connection

Strengthening warmth and security

The first phase focuses on strengthening your relationship with your child. You learn and practice skills intended to help children feel calmer, more secure in their relationships, and more confident in themselves.

02 / Supporting behavior

Calm, consistent limits

The second phase focuses on responding to challenging behaviors with confidence, consistency, and appropriate discipline. Caregivers practice setting limits, guiding behavior, and helping children navigate rules and expectations.

Planning for care

Progress at your family's pace.

With consistent attendance and homework completion, PCIT can be completed in approximately 12–20 sessions. Treatment is not time-limited, and each family's needs may differ.

For more information, visit PCIT International's resource for parents (opens in a new tab).

Who PCIT supports

Typically ages 2–7: Young children and their caregivers.

Ages 8–11: Developmentally appropriate adaptations offered by Milestone therapists.

Connection grows through play.

Theraplay brings children and their caregivers together through playful, nurturing interactions that encourage feelings of safety, joy, and connection.

Explore Theraplay → Contact Our Office
  1. Home
  2. Attachment & Relationships
  3. Theraplay

Understanding Theraplay

A playful approach to emotional and relational well-being.

Theraplay is an evidence-based therapeutic intervention for children ages 0–12 who experience emotional or behavioral challenges and their caregivers.

The approach focuses on the relationship between a child and their caregiver, using guided interactions to help build feelings of safety, care, and connection.

Sometimes connection is strengthened through moments of shared play, comfort, and delight.

When families seek support

When might Theraplay help?

Families may explore Theraplay when children are having difficulty with emotions, behavior, or their relationships with caregivers. Situations described by Milestone include:

01 / Difficult experiences

Rebuilding a sense of security

Disruptions in a child's relationship with a significant caregiver following violence in the home or community, caregiver substance use, sexual abuse, divorce, separation, or loss.

02 / Transitions

Navigating changes in care

Changes in placement or caregivers, including experiences related to foster care.

03 / Emotions

Supporting big feelings

Children showing challenging behaviors or struggling to manage their emotions.

04 / Family well-being

Care through health challenges

Physical or mental health difficulties affecting members of the family.

05 / Relationships

Strengthening your bond

Caregivers who would like support in strengthening their relationship with their child.

What sessions involve

Guided play. Shared connection.

In Theraplay, a therapist guides a caregiver and child through playful games, developmentally challenging activities, and nurturing interactions.

These shared experiences are designed to help caregivers respond to and regulate a child's emotions and behavior while communicating care, joy, delight, and safety.

For more information, visit What Is Theraplay? (opens in a new tab) from the Theraplay organization.

The emphasis is on helping children experience safety and connection in the caregiver–child relationship.

The heart of Theraplay

Helping connection feel safe, joyful, and real.

Through these interactions, children can experience care and connection, which may support their overall functioning and relationships.

Caregivers are active participants in this process, sharing experiences that are centered on the relationship.

What is the goal?

To create opportunities for children and caregivers to experience warmth, understanding, and connection through guided interactions.

Every family's needs and experiences are different.

Trauma-informed care for children & teens / Oakdale, Minnesota

Support after difficult experiences.

Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT) helps children, adolescents, and their caregivers address the emotional impact of trauma, stress, and adversity.

Explore TF-CBT → Contact Our Office
  1. Home
  2. Trauma
  3. Trauma-Focused CBT

Understanding TF-CBT

Helping children and teens process what they have experienced.

Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT) is an evidence-based intervention for children and adolescents ages 6–18 and their caregivers when trauma, stress, or adversity has affected their lives.

The approach brings together trauma-sensitive techniques, cognitive behavioral strategies, family involvement, and supportive therapeutic work to address trauma-related difficulties.

Children and teens deserve support that meets them with understanding and helps them develop ways to cope with difficult experiences.

When families seek support

When might TF-CBT help?

Families may explore TF-CBT when a traumatic or stressful experience has affected a child's emotions, behavior, or relationships.

01 / Emotional well-being

Trauma-related distress

A child or teen is experiencing fear, anxiety, depression, or post-traumatic stress symptoms related to traumatic life events.

02 / Difficult experiences

Single or multiple traumas

A child or adolescent has been impacted by one traumatic experience or by several experiences over time.

03 / Family connection

Caregiver support

Caregivers want guidance with parenting and strengthening the caregiver–child relationship after a traumatic or stressful event.

What treatment involves

Practical skills and trauma-sensitive support.

TF-CBT uses a range of approaches to help children and adolescents better understand their experiences and develop skills for responding to difficult emotions.

01 / Understanding

Understanding trauma

Age-appropriate education helps children and teens make sense of trauma and its effects.

02 / Regulation

Calming & emotional regulation

Developing calming strategies and skills for recognizing and managing strong emotions.

03 / Coping

Helpful ways of thinking

Learning and practicing cognitive coping strategies to respond to thoughts and feelings more adaptively.

04 / Processing

Processing difficult experiences

Support for understanding and integrating traumatic or stressful experiences in a healthy way.

Supporting caregivers

Caregiver involvement matters, too.

TF-CBT includes participation by a non-offending caregiver. The approach can support caregivers in managing their own distress about the child's traumatic experiences while building effective parenting skills and supportive interactions.

Support extends beyond the session.

Support for a young person can also include strengthening the understanding and responsiveness of the adults around them.

Learn more through the National Child Traumatic Stress Network's TF-CBT resource (opens in a new tab).

Helping children feel safe and connected.

Child-Parent Psychotherapy (CPP) supports young children and their caregivers as they make sense of difficult experiences and strengthen the relationships around them.

Understanding child-parent psychotherapy

Support that includes both child and caregiver.

Trauma-Informed Child-Parent Psychotherapy is an evidence-based therapeutic intervention for young children from birth through age seven and their caregivers.

CPP aims to help young children understand difficult events their family has experienced, develop ways to cope with challenging emotions, and have a clearer sense of what they can expect in the future.

At the heart of CPP is attention to the child’s experiences and the strengths and relationships within the family.

When families seek support

When might CPP help?

There are many reasons a family might seek support following a difficult experience or a change in a child’s relationships and daily life.

01 / Loss & separation

Difficult life events

Loss of a loved one, separation, or other frightening or painful events.

02 / Trauma

Frightening experiences

Serious medical procedures or experiences of abuse or violence at home or in the community.

03 / Emotional well-being

Emotional and behavioral challenges

Challenging behaviors or difficulties managing emotions.

04 / Family transitions

Changes in caregiving

Changes in a child's placement or caregivers.

05 / Family health

Health-related stress

Physical or mental health difficulties affecting family members.

06 / Relationships

Caregiver–child connection

Caregivers who want support with parenting and their relationship with their child.

What treatment involves

Care for the family, together and individually.

CPP is delivered through a combination of caregiver-only sessions and caregiver–child family sessions. The approach supports a family's strengths and relationships while respecting the knowledge caregivers bring about their own children.

01 / Supporting caregivers

Caregiver-only sessions

Caregivers have space within treatment to focus on their child's experiences and their family's needs.

02 / Connecting together

Caregiver–child sessions

Family sessions bring the child and caregiver together as part of the therapeutic process.

Family-centered care

Care that builds on your family’s strengths.

CPP brings caregivers and children into the therapeutic process while making room for each family’s experiences, relationships, and needs.

For young children and caregivers.

CPP provides trauma-informed support for children from birth through age seven and their caregivers.
